# html-to-pdf calibration evidence

Generated by `python tests/fixtures/html_to_pdf/_calibrate.py` after
`python tests/fixtures/html_to_pdf/_generate.py`.

Every row is the real pipeline (intake guards -> render in an isolated
child -> output validation), so these numbers are reproducible instead of
quoted from a chat log. Each served fixture is rendered twice and the
second pass is compared against the first, so a number that drifts between
runs is reported instead of committed. Per-row wall-clock times are
deliberately absent for the same reason: they measure the load of the
machine, not the behavior of the code, so timing appears once as a
conservative bucket below.

- PyMuPDF `1.26.3`, Python `3.11.9` on `Windows`
- Ink metric: DeviceGray pixmap at `36` dpi; samples >= `251` are paper, everything else is ink
- Ceilings under test: input `512000` bytes, depth `500`, token `1000`, pages `500`, render timeout `20` s, ink floor `1`
- Double-render check: 12 served fixtures rendered a second time; pages, ink totals and unresolved image counts matched exactly

## What the separation proves

- Visually-empty documents that passed structural validation and were still refused: `blank.html`=0, `hidden_display_none.html`=0, `nbsp_only.html`=0, `script_generated_body.html`=0, `tiny_font.html`=0, `white_on_white.html`=0, `whitespace_only.html`=0.
- Smallest ink total among served documents: `3` (`one_dot.html`).
- Every empty case measures exactly 0 ink while every served document reaches at least 1, which is why the floor is 1: a higher floor starts refusing legitimate minimal pages while catching nothing additional.
- `page_break_blank_tail.html` totals 8,134 ink while its least-ink page measures 0: a per-page rule would wrongly refuse it, the document total accepts it.
- The heaviest legitimate document is `just_under_ceiling.html` (510,994 bytes, 126 pages). Every document that spawns a child rendered in under 2 s including child start-up, which is what makes the 20 s render timeout at least a 10x margin rather than a guess.

## Known rendering limits measured here (disclosed on the landing page)

- `css_flexbox_layout.html` keeps its text but ignores flex/grid/float layout.
- `external_image_only.html` renders MuPDF's `[image]` placeholder instead of the network image: it is served (placeholders are not a failure) and the `unresolved <img>` column is the observability signal behind the landing-page caveat that images work only as data-URIs.
- `script_generated_body.html` produces no ink at all: JavaScript is not executed.
